name: French Boeuf Bourguignon
description: Boeuf bourguignon and coq au vin are genuinely close siblings from Burgundy, the same real technique with a different protein - both depend on real beurre manié, softened butter kneaded together with flour into a smooth paste and whisked into the sauce at the very end, not a roux made at the start, which is what gives the finished sauce its real glossy, velvety sheen. Real technique marinates the beef in wine overnight, and the classic garniture bourguignonne of pearl onions, mushrooms, and real bacon is added only at the finish.

ingredients_full.note: small-diced, standing in for pearl onions

ingredients.note: small-diced, standing in for pearl onions

steps_detailed: Marinate the beef in the wine overnight in the refrigerator, if time allows.
Remove the beef, pat dry, and brown in half the butter, 8-9 minutes.
Add the bacon and onion, and cook 4-5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste, bay leaf, and the wine marinade, and simmer 2-2.5 hours, until the beef is completely tender.
Knead the remaining butter with the flour into a smooth paste (beurre manié).
Whisk the beurre manié into the simmering sauce a little at a time at the very end - real technique adds this last, not at the start, for a glossy, velvety finish.

name: French Coq au Vin
description: Coq au vin, chicken braised in red wine, shares real technique and garniture with boeuf bourguignon - the same real beurre manié thickens the sauce at the end, but the chicken braises for closer to an hour rather than several hours.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 8-9 minutes, in half the butter.
Add the bacon and onion, and cook 4-5 minutes.
Add the wine and bay leaf, and simmer 45-50 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Knead the remaining butter with the flour into a smooth paste.
Whisk the beurre manié into the sauce at the very end for a glossy finish.

name: French Ratatouille
description: Ratatouille, a real vegetable stew from Provence, is genuinely built by cooking each vegetable separately before combining, so each keeps its own real texture rather than turning to mush together.
steps_detailed: Cook the eggplant in half the olive oil separately, 6-7 minutes, until softened, then set aside.
Cook the zucchini and bell pepper separately in the remaining oil, 5-6 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the garlic and tomatoes together 8-10 minutes into a sauce.
Combine everything and simmer 8-10 minutes more - real technique keeps each vegetable's own texture rather than cooking them all together from the start.

name: French Onion Soup
description: French onion soup depends genuinely on the real, patient caramelization of the onions - real technique cooks them low and slow for 45 minutes or more, until they turn a deep mahogany brown, which is what builds the soup's real depth.

ingredients_full.ingredient: 365 (Whole Foods) 365 Everyday Value, White Hamburger Buns

ingredients.ingredient: 365 (Whole Foods) 365 Everyday Value, White Hamburger Buns

steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the butter over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, 45-50 minutes, until deeply, darkly caramelized - real French onion soup depends on this real patience.
Add the broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Ladle into a bowl, top with the toasted bread and cheese, and broil 2-3 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.

name: French Quiche Lorraine
description: Quiche lorraine, a real egg custard tart with bacon and cheese, depends on real technique blind-baking the crust first so it doesn't turn soggy under the filling.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and butter with a little cold water into a firm dough, press into a tart pan, and blind-bake at 375F (190C) for 12-15 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, cream, and cheese together, and stir in the bacon.
Pour into the baked crust and bake at 350F (175C) for 25-28 minutes until just set.

name: French Crème Brûlée
description: Crème brûlée, a real baked custard with a caramelized sugar top, depends on real technique torching or broiling the sugar right before serving, so the contrast between the hot, crackling top and the cold custard beneath is at its sharpest.
steps_detailed: Whisk the egg yolks with half the sugar and the vanilla.
Warm the cream gently, then whisk into the egg mixture.
Pour into ramekins and bake in a water bath at 325F (165C) for 30-35 minutes until just set.
Chill at least 2 hours.
Sprinkle the remaining sugar over the top and caramelize with a torch or under the broiler right before serving.

name: French Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting France's Mediterranean and Atlantic coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

description: A simple mustard vinaigrette, the real, everyday French salad dressing, real technique whisking the mustard in first to help emulsify the oil and vinegar together.
steps_detailed: Whisk the mustard and vinegar together first, then slowly whisk in the olive oil until emulsified.
